Evenitto
Discover and plan local events and activities across the Netherlands
Evenitto is an event calendar for the whole Netherlands in English and Dutch. It collects listings from hundreds of venues, city calendars, and organizers, so you can see what's on tonight, this weekend, or during school holidays. You can filter events by city, date, price (including free), age, and type, such as concerts, theatre, workshops, family outings, and exhibitions. Each listing links to the official organizer for tickets. The site also features profiles for over 100 concert halls and theatres, plus a blog with practical guides like Oktoberfest dates by city and free Christmas markets.

Inbox Works
The simplest shared inbox for teams answering customer email together
When a team answers customer email together, issues often arise: an email goes unanswered, a promised follow-up is forgotten, two people reply to the same message, or an email is forwarded to another app just to discuss it. Inbox Works keeps track of replies and keeps the team's discussion beside the email, where the customer never sees it, on the address you already use. No tickets. Add-ons like Hand off bring in more when your team needs it, without complicating the inbox. Early access is free; try the demo with a sample team, no sign-up. Google and Microsoft mailbox connections are planned.

drip
A live water meter for Claude Code and Codex CLI
I made drip because no AI provider publishes water usage per token. It estimates the water your AI coding agent uses and shows it live while you work, built from published research (ML.ENERGY, Microsoft, Google, Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, CACM) with every coefficient linked to its source. It includes a water meter in the Claude Code status line, a live meter beside Codex CLI via 'drip run codex', and a browser breakdown by model with low, mid, and high range plus 30-day history. Token counts come from your agent's logs; water is estimated, so it shows a range. It runs locally, requires no account, sends no telemetry, and is free under the MIT license.
